dct_description_sm: The communities of Ahousaht and Tla-o-qui-aht First Nations are located in Clayoquot Sound, on the Central Pacific Coast of Vancouver Island, British Columbia. These communities initiated a process to increase their adaptability to climate change in 2010 by creating a community and ecosystem-based Climate Change Adaptation Plan. During their climate adaptation planning process numerous adaptation objectives and measures were identified. As they cannot undertake all of these measures simultaneously, they have, as a community, chosen to focus on the following priorities: 1) Wild/Traditional Food Security Planning, 2) Fisheries Diversification Planning, and 3) Shoreline & infrastructure Vulnerability and Adaptation Planning. Wild foods are crucial to the culture and health of the Clayoquot Nations and yet are seriously threatened with climate change. A number of commercial fish species are also at risk due to climate change; and coastal shorelines are already eroding and will continue to do so as a result of climate change putting remote community (particularly island based) infrastructure and housing at risk.
